transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-20
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Alice Park, Samir Patel, Miguel Ortega, Noah Kim (Redwood) — Dr. Lena Morris, Ravi Kapoor, Tasha Nguyen, Marta Lopez, Ethan Shaw (BlueQuill)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be brief):
- Sprint-zero intake for BlueQuill therapeutic inference pilot.
- Discussed deployment preference (Dedicated vs Private VPC), security checklist, SSO, and initial success metrics.
- Agreed next steps to provision pilot infra and share security docs + pricing estimate.

Topics: onboarding runbook, VPC/private deployment, SLA/timelines, SOC2/KMS, telemetry and rollback plan, pilot success criteria

Action items (recap): see metadata action_items above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alice Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we are, uh, excited to kick off sprint zero with BlueQuill. Quick intro, I'm Alice, your CSM at Redwood.
[01:00] Dr. Lena Morris: Hi Alice, thanks. I'm Lena, CTO. We have Ravi, Tasha, Marta and Ethan on — we'll be driving the pilot from our side.
[02:00] Alice Park: Great, can each BlueQuill person just say their primary goal for the pilot very briefly?
[03:00] Ravi Kapoor: For us it's throughput and reproducible latency for batch inference and then a safe path to production with auditability. Cost is important but reliability first.
[04:00] Tasha Nguyen: Infosec priorities: encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention, and data residency controls.
[05:00] Marta Lopez: ML team wants checkpointing for KV cache, ability to pin model versions, and a simple eval harness to detect quality regressions.
[06:00] Samir Patel: Perfect, that lines up with Redwood features. We support model pinning, rollout policies, and we have a built-in eval runner—we'll walk through that in the technical deep dive.
[07:00] Ethan Shaw: On infra, our preference is a VPC/private deployment in us-west-2 due to data egress policy; wondering what the network setup looks like.
[08:00] Miguel Ortega: We usually do a private control plane with customer VPC peering or Transit Gateway. For sprint zero we can provision Dedicated capacity inside your VPC or set up a Private deployment package — we'll send a diagram.
[09:00] Dr. Lena Morris: Clarify: Dedicated inside our VPC vs Redwood Dedicated — are there differences in isolation and audit?
[10:00] Samir Patel: Yes, good question. Dedicated (Redwood) is dedicated GPU pools managed by us but can be configured with customer VPC peering and strict network ACLs; Private (on-prem/VPC) gives you the control plane in your network. We'll outline trade-offs: operational overhead vs absolute control.
[11:00] Tasha Nguyen: We need to know SOC2 compatibility and if Redwood can forward audit logs to our SIEM. Also which fields in logs are PII/masked.
[12:00] Alice Park: We are SOC2 Type II; we can forward audit logs — Samir will capture log schema and retention options. We also support log redaction configs.
[13:00] Marta Lopez: On the model side, we plan to serve two encoder-decoder models — one smaller for low-latency replies, one larger for higher-quality generation. Any constraints re quantization / KV cache?
[14:00] Samir Patel: Quantization is supported — we have optimized kernels; you can expect different throughput curves. We'll include an estimated tokens/sec profile for both models. KV cache checkpointing works across pod restarts but you want sticky sessions for best effect.
[15:00] Ethan Shaw: What about secrets? KMS/HSM integration? We need to route keys to our HSM.
[16:00] Miguel Ortega: We integrate with common KMS providers, and for Private you'll manage KMS; for Dedicated we can integrate into your KMS via kms-connector and key-wrapping flows. We'll document expected IAM roles.
[17:00] Dr. Lena Morris: Timeline: we want a pilot in prod-like environment within three weeks. Is that feasible?
[18:00] Alice Park: Three weeks is tight but doable for sprint zero if we get VPC details and SSO/KMS info quickly. That's why we suggested immediate action items today.
[19:00] Ravi Kapoor: Success metrics for pilot: 99th percentile latency under 350ms for small model at 50 qps; throughput of 5k tokens/sec for batched workloads; and no regression in our eval prompt suite.
[20:00] Samir Patel: We'll map those criteria to a performance test plan. For latency SLOs we need to understand average sequence length and percent of streaming calls — is that mostly chat or batch?
[21:00] Marta Lopez: 60% chat (streaming), 40% batch. Avg sequence length 80 tokens chat, 600 tokens batch.
[22:00] Samir Patel: Good — that helps kernel selection and batching profiles. We'll propose concurrency settings and suggested batch sizes.
[23:00] Alice Park: On the operational side, who will be primary on-call for BlueQuill during pilot?
[24:00] Ethan Shaw: Likely me and Marta for the ML side; Tasha for security escalations.
[25:00] Tasha Nguyen: We also want RBAC so only a small set can rotate keys or change rollout policies.
[26:00] Miguel Ortega: Redwood Console supports token-level RBAC and route-level permissions. We'll show default roles; you can also map to SAML groups for SCIM sync.
[27:00] Dr. Lena Morris: Any blockers you anticipate? Network, capacity, or compliance?
[28:00] Samir Patel: Mostly network (peering and firewall holes) and SSO mapping; both are straightforward but need work on your side. If you have strict air-gap requirements we'd need more time for on-prem packaging.
[29:00] Ravi Kapoor: We do not need air-gap for sprint zero; VPC peering is acceptable. We might look at an on-prem option later.
[30:00] Alice Park: Let's talk telemetry and billing: you'll get token-level cost breakdown and a per-route latency dashboard. Any specific retention needs?
[31:00] Tasha Nguyen: Security wants 12 months of audit logs, and perf telemetry for 3 months. Can Redwood support that?
[32:00] Miguel Ortega: Yes, retention tiers are available; 12 months for audit logs is on our enterprise tier, we'll call that out in the pricing estimate.
[33:00] Marta Lopez: For the eval harness, can we upload a prompt set and get automated regression alerts?
[34:00] Samir Patel: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes eval monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll enable it for your pilot so any drift triggers an alerting workflow to Slack/email.
[35:00] Ethan Shaw: For provisioning, what credentials do you need from us to spin up pilot nodes in our VPC?
[36:00] Miguel Ortega: We'll need a service account with limited IAM permissions for VPC peering, a list of CIDR ranges, and the KMS key ARN if we're integrating. We'll send a minimal permissions doc.
[37:00] Dr. Lena Morris: About training data: none of our sensitive patient PII will be sent to model training, right? We need confirmation.
[38:00] Alice Park: Correct — inference only; we have data usage and retention policies. We'll provide the legal snippet and a DPA addendum if needed.
[39:00] Tasha Nguyen: Also want to check encryption in transit details. TLS version, mutual TLS support?
[40:00] Samir Patel: TLS 1.2+ supported, and for Private we can enable mTLS to your internal CA. We'll include mTLS steps in the network diagram.
[41:00] Ravi Kapoor: Do you support canary rollouts / automatic fallback if a model starts regressing?
[42:00] Miguel Ortega: Yes — rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant. We'll show how to configure thresholds and health checks.
[43:00] Marta Lopez: Anything about tokenization differences causing eval mismatch? We've seen differing tokenizers between open models.
[44:00] Samir Patel: Good call — tokenizer mismatches can cause eval flakiness. We'll recommend canonical tokenization at ingest and provide a mapping utility.
[45:00] Alice Park: Wrap up — let's confirm the earliest dates: SSO docs by 10/22, runbook by 10/21, pilot infra provision by 10/27, tech deep-dive week of 10/27. Does that align?
[46:00] Dr. Lena Morris: Yes, that works. Also please include a cost sensitivity table showing latency vs cost tradeoffs — we want to review with finance.
[47:00] Samir Patel: We'll include a spreadsheet with three profiles: conservative, balanced, and aggressive — showing expected unit costs and 95/99 latency estimates.
[48:00] Alice Park: Thank you all. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive and circulate the docs. Final quick Qs?
[48:30] Tasha Nguyen: One last — can Redwood support forwarding logs to Splunk?
[48:45] Samir Patel: Yes, Splunk forwarder is supported; we'll include config.
[49:00] Alice Park: Great — thanks everyone, talk soon.
